function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current temperature and humidity for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to get the weather for.

include_temperature.description: Whether to include the temperature in the result. Default is true.

include_humidity.description: Whether to include the humidity in the result. Default is true.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "If I want to include temperature and humidity in the result, what are the current temperature and humidity for New York, Los Angeles, London, and Tokyo?" They want to use the function get_current_weather. We need to call the function for each location. The function signature: get_current_weather(location: string, include_temperature?: boolean, include_humidity?: boolean). We should set both include_temperature and include_humidity to true (default is true). So we can call the function once with location "New York" etc. But the function returns data for one location. We need to call it four times. The user wants all four. So we need to call the function four times. The assistant should call the function for each location. The function returns JSON. We need to output the results. The user didn't specify format. We can just output the results. We'll call the function for each location.
